questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Amsterdam due partly to academic opportunities, since they have some nice urban planning courses available, and party due to Amsterdam being a very international city with a lot of international students, meaning that i could get by fine with English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! I didn't have any problems.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During the introduction week, the university hosted a practical matters day, where international students could get everything they needed done, or get information on how to get it done. The exchange office was also pretty helpful if you contacted them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a couple different options available, both on and off campus. I lived in the dorms in Uilenstede, which i highly recommend! The dorms were not the prettiest and not in the greatest condition, but they were very social, so it was easy to get to know a lot of people, and most of my friends were from the dorm. As far as i heard from the people who lived there, the other options both more expensive and less social.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We shared a kitchen, which was not the best but decent enough. We were 12 people, so it could get pretty dirty, so make sure to make a good cleaning schedule. Also, for some reason none of the dorms have ovens. We bought a used toaster oven, which worked decently, but i definitely missed a proper oven.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Make sure to pay the housing fee as quickly as possible! Housing is allocated on a first-come first-served basis, and you get access to the website where you book the housing based on when you paid the housing fee.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only downside was the general condition of the dorms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before registering for courses, you have to apply for approval for the courses you'd like, after which you can register for the courses you were approved for. You can both choose a minor or individual courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a catalog of all the courses available to exchange students in the different faculties. Other than that, the exchange team were pretty easy to contact if you had any questions or problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first, i only got approved for 2 of the 8 courses i applied for. However, after some back and forth with the exchange team, i got approved for all but one course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you think you are eligible for the courses, make sure to ask again if you at first don't get approval! They overlooked some things in the first approval, but were pretty helpful once i asked again.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For the most part i really enjoyed the courses i took! There were a lot of very interesting courses available, and since you could choose five, you could try a lot of different things.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level and workload of some of the courses was pretty low. In some ways this was pretty nice, since it meant i had time to do a lot of other stuff than just study, but for some of the courses the level was so low, that the courses were kind of unmotivating/uninteresting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar, especially for the courses from the social science faculty. There was a lot less group work though, and all the exams were individual except for one group presentation, which only made out a small percentage of our grade. Also, there were more multiple choice/essay based exams instead of the papers/projects i'm used to from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really loved Development and Globalization! The professor was really passionate and engaging, and the course material was really interesting.

I also loved Urban Culture and Public Space. The professor was very engaging, and the course material was really interesting. For this course we had to write a paper based on fieldwork on a public space, which was really fun!

I also really liked Urbanism and Landscape Architecture. The course material was very interesting, although the lectures were kind of boring, because they pretty much just went through the chapters assigned for each week. For this course we had to write a paper on the development of a city, which was also really fun!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not much. Going out was pretty expensive both due to drinks being expensive and due to public transport stopping pretty early outside of the weekends, so we had to take ubers home quite often.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Overall i think it was pretty similar to Copenhagen. I spent more on food, but i think that might have just been because i treated myself a bit haha

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some clubs available at the university, however i didn't really participate in them. There was a really nice gym though which had a lot of classes such as spinning, kickboxing, yoga, poledancing etc. There is also a buddy program, which i did actually sign up for. I think it was a pretty nice way of getting to know people, although i met a lot of people at the dorms, so after a while i didn't really participate in the activities through the program.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get a museum card! Amsterdam has a lot of really nice museums, and they can get quite expensive, so even though the museum card seems expensive at first, it pays for itself pretty quickly. Also, i really enjoyed the gym and the classes you could take through it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam has a lot to see and do! I spent most of my weekends either going out, going to museums or going to some of the many markets (can recommend IJ Hallen). Otherwise, the Netherlands has a lot of really nice cities that are worth a visit! I only went to a few, but wish i went to more.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Culturally, Denmark and the Netherlands are very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Good luck haha. I don't know, it can be pretty difficult unless you make a lot of effort. They are pretty nice though! There are so many exchange students though, so i mostly hung out with other internationals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: For the international students, i really liked how open everyone was to meeting new people and making new experiences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open! There are so many people from a lot of different backgrounds that you can learn a lot from.

Make the most of your time. It is pretty easy to get caught up in schoolwork, but make sure to take time to see and experience the city! There were a lot of things that i wanted to do, but never got around to. It can be a good idea to make lists of what you want to see and do, and don't be afraid of asking people if they want to join!

Enjoy it! Exchange is an amazing and unique opportunity. Before you know, it's over :'(

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Probably obvious, but get a bike! Public transport is really expensive and biking around is a nice way to experience the city. You can find really cheap used ones online, although they can be pretty sketchy. Otherwise, Swapfiets is a good option.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people from all over the world. You make a lot of friends from different places, and visiting is a good excuse if you ever want to travel:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having your usual support system and saying goodbye once it's all over.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
